sections.name: Software Engineering
sections.outcome: Produce correct, maintainable software changes from bounded function implementations through repository-scale diagnosis, implementation, verification, packaging, and version-control integration.
includes: Synthesizing executable code from behavioral specifications
Diagnosing, repairing, extending, testing, and restructuring software
Managing dependency, build, release, and version-control concerns that accompany code changes
excludes: Product analysis that does not culminate in a software change
Pure system administration outside a repository or build
Hardware instruction scheduling without software implementation

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement a small documented function that transforms a list of records and add focused examples for its empty, singleton, and ordinary cases.

Deliver one optional parser plugin for an unfamiliar packaged command-line project: trace its extension path, implement the specified behavior, extract shared dispatch logic, add focused and command-level tests, declare and build the optional package extra, and integrate the change on a topic branch after resolving a conflicting upstream edit.

sections.name: Standalone Function Synthesis
sections.outcome: Translate a self-contained behavioral contract into an executable function whose algorithm, data transformations, and edge-case behavior satisfy that contract.
excludes: Changes that require navigating an existing repository
Repairs whose implementation must be localized from a symptom

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement a function that returns whether any integer in a sequence is outside a supplied inclusive range.

Implement one function that validates timestamped label records for conflicting identifiers, aggregates numeric readings by normalized label, orders the groups deterministically, and returns a compact textual summary.

sections.name: Search and Predicate Functions
sections.outcome: Implement boolean functions that decide a stated property by examining elements, pairs, or local relationships without missing boundary cases.
excludes: Repairing predicates inside an existing system

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement a function that reports whether a sequence contains a negative integer.

Implement a function that reports whether a token stream contains either a repeated token within a configurable window or a forbidden adjacent pair, handling empty streams and exact window boundaries.

sections.name: Collection Transformation and Aggregation
sections.outcome: Implement functions that select, transform, group, aggregate, or order collection elements into the specified result shape.
includes: Sorting structured elements by derived keys
excludes: Functions whose only result is a boolean decision

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement a function that returns the count of values in each category of an input sequence.

Implement a function that filters invalid transactions, groups the remainder by account, computes each account's total and median amount, and returns records ordered by descending total with a deterministic tie break.

sections.name: Constructive String Functions
sections.outcome: Implement functions that inspect string structure and construct the minimal or canonical string required by a specification.
excludes: General text parsing into repository state
Formatting repairs to an existing public API

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement a function that collapses each nonempty run of whitespace to one space while preserving non-whitespace characters.
Implement a reversible run-length encoder that emits the shortest valid representation under the supplied escaping rules and correctly handles digits, escape characters, and single-character runs.

sections.name: Repository Investigation and Behavioral Evidence
sections.outcome: Trace observable behavior through an unfamiliar repository and establish focused and public-workflow tests that expose the relevant contract.
includes: Locating public entry points and responsible implementation paths
Following state, control flow, data flow, and side effects
Creating focused and integrated tests with observable assertions
excludes: Choosing or implementing the final repair
Tests that merely prove code executes

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a documented public method to the helper that computes its result and add one assertion to the existing focused test for that result.

For one command whose generated manifest is wrong, trace the same execution from argument parsing through configuration and persistence, then create a focused test at the responsible boundary and a command-level test that exposes the manifest defect.

sections.name: Behavior Tracing and Fault Localization
sections.outcome: Follow a public symptom through entry points, dispatch, state transitions, and side effects to identify the smallest responsible code boundary.
includes: Searching definitions, call sites, and configuration consumers
Tracing parser, callback, resolver, and command paths
Comparing expected and actual state transitions
excludes: Performance profiling without a functional symptom

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one public method call to the helper that computes its return value.
Trace a missing command-side effect through configuration loading, dispatch, callbacks, and persistence, and identify the smallest boundary at which execution diverges from the documented contract.

sections.name: Behavioral Test Authoring
sections.outcome: Write focused and integrated tests that distinguish compliant behavior from a defect through public values, state, events, files, or repository effects.
includes: Deterministic regression tests at component boundaries
excludes: Assertions coupled only to private call counts
Live external services when a local boundary suffices

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one assertion to an existing test that distinguishes the documented result from the current result.
For one stateful import command, use a shared isolated workspace to write a focused test for its state transition and a public command test for the resulting output file and persisted state.

sections.name: Focused Regression Tests
sections.outcome: Create small deterministic tests that isolate one semantic rule or state contract and distinguish faulty behavior from corrected behavior.
includes: Assertions on values, ordering, identity, and exceptions

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a failing assertion for one documented boundary input to an existing component test.
Write a compact parameterized suite for a date-window classifier covering containment, partial overlap, touching endpoints, reversed input order, empty windows, and disjoint windows.

sections.name: Integrated Workflow Tests
sections.outcome: Test contracts that emerge across public APIs, callbacks, commands, files, generated artifacts, or multiple modules.
includes: Temporary filesystem, database, and schema fixtures
Assertions on cross-component state and side effects
excludes: Live network dependencies when local substitutes exist
Tests that inspect only internal calls

sample_tasks.instruction: Run one public command in an isolated temporary workspace and assert its documented file effect.

Build an isolated workflow fixture that invokes a public import command, crosses configuration and persistence boundaries, and verifies returned data, emitted output, generated files, and final repository state.

sections.name: Boundary and Predicate Contract Repair
sections.outcome: Diagnose and correct a deterministic predicate or boundary convention while preserving all unaffected cases.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a public boundary-classification failure to its predicate, create focused cases for both sides of the boundary, and correct one comparison operator.

Trace a scheduling library's incorrect window-conflict result to its normalized range predicate, add focused coverage for overlap, containment, touching endpoints, empty windows, reversed operands, and disjoint windows, then repair the predicate without changing neighboring scheduling behavior.

sections.name: Identity and Mutable-State Contract Repair
sections.outcome: Restore intended object identity and mutation visibility across accessors, nested contexts, decorators, and repeated calls.
includes: Live mutable mappings when mutation is contractual
Shared state across parent and child contexts
excludes: Global mutable state introduced as a shortcut

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace repeated reads of a public mapping property, prove with a focused test that mutations are lost, and change the accessor so the same underlying mapping remains visible.

Trace metadata from creation through nested contexts and decorator-mediated access, write focused identity and mutation tests, and repair the storage contract so changes persist through command execution without leaking between independent contexts.

sections.name: Evaluation Context Repair
sections.outcome: Restore correct compilation and evaluation behavior while preserving the documented global, local, and expression context.
includes: Compilation modes and executable object kinds

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a public expression method to its compilation call, add focused tests for a literal and a captured name, and replace the incorrect compilation mode.

Trace an expression environment through capture, compilation, and evaluation, add focused cases for arithmetic, captured locals, module-qualified functions, and invalid statements, then restore expression evaluation without changing namespace precedence.

sections.name: Collection Ordering Contract Repair
sections.outcome: Restore one documented traversal order consistently across direct iteration and all related collection views.
includes: Consistency among keys, values, items, and iteration
excludes: Sorting APIs that intentionally choose a new order

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace reversed public iteration to the index traversal, add focused assertions for direct iteration and keys, and correct the traversal direction.

Trace an ordered record container's component traversal, add focused tests for sparse positions, replacement, direct iteration, keys, values, and items, and repair the shared ordering mechanism so every view remains consistent.

sections.name: Public API Contract Restoration
sections.outcome: Restore a removed or broken public parameter, return shape, or formatting behavior without turning the repair into a new API design.
includes: Reinstating documented parameters and accepted value forms
Applying restored behavior at the correct output boundary
Preserving calls that omit the restored option

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a documented formatting argument through the public method and output path, establish focused and public failing tests, and restore its constant-string form at the existing rendering boundary.

Trace a missing line-prefix option from a documented public method through multiline rendering, add focused tests for constant and callback values plus a public formatting workflow, and restore both forms while leaving default output byte-for-byte unchanged.

sections.name: Input and Resolution Pipeline Repair
sections.outcome: Repair a staged input path so extraction, representation detection, identifier decoding, dispatch, and resolution agree on one public contract.
includes: Consistent encoding, decoding, and object lookup

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one public import through extraction and dispatch, establish focused and public failing tests, and correct the single extraction step that drops an optional field.

For one resource-reference importer, trace and test a shared reference from text extraction through representation detection, identifier decoding, handler dispatch, and final object lookup, then repair the inconsistent stages so the public import resolves the intended resource.

sections.name: Structured Parsing Repair
sections.outcome: Correct tokenization or field extraction so structured text produces the documented normalized representation.
excludes: Selecting a parser from a file type
Adding a new grammar or serialization form

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace an optional-title failure through a public parse call, add focused titled and untitled cases, and fix the extraction of that field.

Trace reference-definition parsing to its environment update, add focused cases for escaped labels, normalized destinations, optional titles, whitespace variants, and multiple definitions, and repair the parser without consuming unrelated text.

sections.name: Format Detection and Dispatch Repair
sections.outcome: Restore correct recognition and dispatch of supported inputs across validation, file inspection, parser selection, and public loading.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a documented file variant from the public loader through validation, add focused and public failing tests, and correct the branch that prevents it from reaching its existing reader.

Trace several variants of one supported scientific format through validation, inspection, reader selection, and public loading, add focused dispatch and end-to-end fixtures, and repair the path while retaining clear rejection of unsupported inputs.

sections.name: Encoding and Resolver Consistency
sections.outcome: Align identifier generation, decoding, type lookup, and object resolution around one round-trip contract.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one generated identifier through its public resolver, add focused round-trip and public query tests, and correct the component that decodes to the wrong type key.

Trace a global identifier from generation through decoding, type lookup, and polymorphic query resolution, add focused round trips for several types and identifiers plus executable public queries, and repair the shared contract.

sections.name: Lifecycle Event Restoration
sections.outcome: Reconnect missing logs, signals, or callbacks to the correct processing stage without duplicating, reordering, or otherwise changing core work.
includes: Locating the lifecycle hook that owns an event
Preserving status, method, and resource context
Testing event level, multiplicity, and ordering
excludes: Changing processing solely to manufacture a message

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a successful public request through its lifecycle hooks, establish focused and workflow tests for the missing event, and restore one emission at the existing completion hook.

Trace one request through redirect, response, retry, and failure stages, add focused hook tests and a public workflow test for contextual event order and multiplicity, and restore reporting without changing request handling.

sections.name: Heterogeneous Operation APIs
sections.outcome: Design and implement a public API that normalizes multiple selection and operation forms into deterministic grouped results.
includes: String operations, callables, and named outputs

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace an established grouped-operation API and its tests, then add one named aggregation over one explicitly selected column while preserving existing calls.

Trace and test an established tabular API, then implement grouped summarization supporting individual columns, column lists, pattern selectors, named outputs, string operations, and callables with deterministic naming and result shape.

sections.name: Declarative Code-Generation Extensions
sections.outcome: Add a bounded declarative attribute and propagate it through syntax parsing, precedence resolution, intermediate representation, and generated output.
includes: Precedence between explicit and inferred values

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one field attribute through parsing and generation, establish focused parser and generated-output tests, and add a literal rename override with documented precedence.

Trace a field-level type override through a compiler plugin's attribute parser, optionality logic, intermediate representation, and target-language emitter, then implement it with focused expansion tests and a public generation test while preserving unannotated fields.

sections.name: Schema-Driven Serialization Features
sections.outcome: Extend a schema and its generated artifacts so field metadata selects and executes the correct structured serialization behavior.
includes: Routing values to structured text or JSON parsers
excludes: Repairing dispatch for an already-supported file format
Ad hoc parsing that bypasses schema metadata
Compiler attributes that affect only generated types

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one field property from schema to runtime configuration and its tests, then add one enum value that selects an existing parser branch.

Trace and test one field's metadata from schema declaration through generated bindings and configuration loading, then add default, structured-text, and JSON forms that route nested values through the corresponding serializers.

sections.name: Asynchronous Coordination Protocols
sections.outcome: Implement asynchronous client adaptation and reusable lease-based ownership coordination with correct cancellation, renewal, loss, release, and callback behavior.
includes: Timed lease state transitions and retries
excludes: Synchronous blocking in the event loop
Consensus algorithms beyond the specified lease protocol

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace an existing synchronous acquisition path and establish focused and public asynchronous tests, then expose one already-nonblocking client operation as a cancellable awaitable.

Using one asynchronous lease client, implement cancellable acquisition and release, then build a leader component on that same lease that renews ownership, handles contention and loss, invokes transition callbacks once, and relinquishes ownership during shutdown.

sections.name: Asynchronous Client Adaptation
sections.outcome: Adapt a stateful client operation to an awaitable interface without blocking the event loop or losing result, exception, timeout, and cancellation semantics.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace one existing client operation and establish focused and public asynchronous tests, then expose that already-nonblocking operation through one awaitable method.
Trace and adapt a lock client's acquisition, timeout, result, exception, cancellation, and release paths into a nonblocking asynchronous interface with deterministic focused and public tests.

sections.name: Lease-Based Ownership Protocols
sections.outcome: Build a reusable asynchronous ownership state machine on a cancellable client adapter, including acquisition, renewal, loss, release, callbacks, and shutdown.
excludes: Implementing the underlying client adapter alone

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement the cancellable acquisition-and-release adapter for a lease client, then add one ownership transition that renews a held lease before expiry and releases it on cancellation.

Implement the full cancellable lease adapter and use it in a leader component that handles contention, renewal, expiration, callback ordering, lease loss, and shutdown without retaining ownership after cancellation.

sections.name: Multi-Module System Synthesis
sections.outcome: Implement a cohesive small system whose modules have explicit dependency direction, testable public interfaces, and coordinated stateful and filesystem behavior.
includes: Separating foundational operations, data processing, and orchestration
Deterministic traversal, aggregation, and side effects
excludes: Placing all logic in one script
Duplicating lower-layer logic in orchestration code
External dependencies when the specification forbids them

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement specified normalization, filtering, aggregation, and ordering functions, place them in a foundational module, and add one dependent module that imports and exposes their combined result.

Implement a standard-library project with a transactional storage module, a depth-bounded file-analysis module that performs deterministic collection transformations, and an orchestration module that applies permissions and returns reports through explicit one-way imports.

sections.name: Refactoring and Code Migration
sections.outcome: Change software structure or interfaces while preserving intended behavior and migrating every affected consumer and artifact.
includes: Changing interfaces with coordinated consumer updates
Migrating schemas, generated code, documentation, tests, and exports
excludes: Leaving compatibility shims without a requirement

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace a duplicated private calculation and establish focused and public behavior tests, then extract it into one shared helper and update both callers.

For one configuration-loading subsystem, trace its callers and establish focused and end-to-end behavior tests, then extract it behind a new module boundary, revise its typed interface, migrate every caller and generated artifact, remove the superseded path, and preserve the same public workflow.

sections.name: Structure-Preserving Refactoring
sections.outcome: Improve function, module, or dependency structure while preserving externally observable behavior.
includes: Maintaining dependency direction and public exports

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace two callers of a repeated calculation and establish focused and public behavior tests, then extract the calculation into one shared function.

Trace a mixed filesystem workflow and establish focused and end-to-end behavior tests, then separate computation, persistence, and orchestration into acyclic modules, remove duplicate implementations, and preserve results and side effects.

sections.name: Cross-Layer Interface Migration
sections.outcome: Migrate an intentional interface change consistently through declarations, implementations, generated artifacts, callers, tests, documentation, and exports.
includes: Updating all consumers and generated bindings
excludes: Backward-compatibility aliases without an explicit requirement

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace every caller of one public parameter and establish focused and public baseline tests, then rename the parameter and update all in-repository consumers without retaining the old name.

Trace a public configuration field through schema, generated bindings, parsers, runtime consumers, exports, examples, and tests, establish behavioral baselines, then replace it with a typed representation and remove the superseded path.

sections.name: Optional Dependency Boundaries
sections.outcome: Keep a package importable and accurately feature-gated when an optional library is present or absent.
includes: Separating annotation-time needs from runtime availability
Lazy or guarded imports at established feature boundaries
Behavior in installed and missing dependency states
excludes: Broad exception handling around arbitrary imports
Dependency version solving and lockfile maintenance

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace an optional library through package import and feature detection, establish focused and package-import tests for both availability states, and move one annotation so it no longer forces the optional import.

Trace an optional rendering feature through package import, capability detection, annotated public APIs, and invocation, add focused and public tests with and without the extra, and repair the boundary so absence fails only when the feature is used.

sections.name: Version-Control-Aware Application Behavior
sections.outcome: Make repository-manipulating application commands create, modify, and stage artifacts exactly as their configuration specifies while preserving unrelated index and working-tree state.
includes: Tracked, untracked, enabled, disabled, and repeated runs

sample_tasks.instruction: Trace an automatic-staging setting through one generation command, establish focused and command-level repository tests, and guard the existing staging call so a generated file remains unstaged when the setting is disabled.

Trace one reproduction command from configuration through manifest, lock, and metric generation to index updates, add focused and repository-level tests, and ensure enabled and disabled modes preserve unrelated staged entries across new, modified, and repeated runs.

sections.name: Build, Packaging, and Dependency Management
sections.outcome: Produce reproducible installable artifacts whose build metadata, dependency constraints, resolved environments, and release contents agree.
excludes: Local installation commands without repository metadata changes

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one missing package-data rule and build an archive that contains the documented resource.

Prepare one library release that adds an optional compression feature: update its dependency constraint and platform marker, refresh the resolved lock, build its wheel and source archive, and confirm the artifacts expose the same metadata and installable contents.

sections.name: Build and Release Artifacts
sections.outcome: Configure and inspect package builds so distributable artifacts contain the intended code, resources, entry points, and metadata.
includes: Package discovery, data files, and entry points

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one resource directory to package metadata and build an archive containing it.
Configure a multi-package command-line project so its wheel and source archive contain the intended modules, templates, license metadata, and executable entry point, with no development-only files.

sections.name: Dependency Constraints and Lockfiles
sections.outcome: Express dependency requirements and produce a consistent resolved environment across supported features and platforms.
includes: Version ranges, extras, and environment markers
Lockfile updates tied to declared requirements
excludes: Updating a lockfile without changing or checking its declared inputs

sample_tasks.instruction: Add one platform marker to an existing dependency constraint and refresh the affected lock entry.
Revise a library's core and optional dependency ranges to remove a resolution conflict across two supported interpreter versions, regenerate the lock, and keep unrelated resolved packages unchanged.

sections.name: Version Control Operations
sections.outcome: Use branches, commits, merges, rebases, and history inspection to integrate changes while preserving intended content and a comprehensible repository history.
includes: History inspection, selective application, and safe correction
excludes: Application code that conditionally stages generated files
Deleting local changes to obtain a clean state

sample_tasks.instruction: Create a topic branch, commit one focused change, and update it with a non-conflicting change from the main branch.

Integrate a three-commit topic branch after the main branch independently edits the same configuration and test files: inspect both histories, rebase or merge deliberately, resolve the semantic conflicts, preserve both intended behaviors, and leave a coherent final history without discarding unrelated work.
